speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Jackson Lam asked whether gender-specific prevention and rehabilitation strategies are needed for women drug abusers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: SPS adopts a gender-responsive and trauma-informed approach for women inmates, including women drug abusers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: SPS' effective gender-specific programming for women inmates received international recognition when it was awarded the Reducing Reoffending Award from the International Corrections and Prisons Association last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik asked how mental health data and integrated support services are utilised to reduce recidivism.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: SPS assesses all inmates admitted to prison and DRC, on the state of their physical and mental health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: SPS partners IMH to support the rehabilitation needs of inmates with mental health conditions and special needs, including referral for assessment to the Prison Psychiatrist from IMH.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Inmates with complex needs are referred to a multi-disciplinary team for appropriate interventions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To support their reintegration, SPS partners community agencies to ensure continued medical care and support after release.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I will now touch on rehabilitation and reintegration efforts for inmates generally, which Mr Patrick Tay, Mr Gabriel Lam, Mr Christopher de Souza and Ms Cassandra Lee have filed cuts on.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This continues to be one of the lowest two-year recidivism rates internationally.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The two-year rate is a proxy indicator of the effectiveness of in-prison programmes and reintegration services available for ex-offenders immediately after release.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The five-year rate is a measure of the sustainable ecosystem of community and family support for ex-offenders to prevent re-offending in the long term.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This cannot be done by SPS or the Government alone and requires strong community support to increase human, social, economic and community capital of inmates, ex-offenders and their families.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: SPS has set out in Corrections 2030, its comprehensive strategies to reduce re-offending in the longer term.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This involves strengthening the families of inmates, maximising the employability and career opportunities of inmates and ex-offenders, and mobilising community partners to support rehabilitation and reintegration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will monitor and track the initiatives rolled out under these strategies to measure its effectiveness and impact.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The building of economic capital, through education and skills training, is important for successful rehabilitation and reintegration, enhancing inmates' ability to secure jobs after release.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: SPS and Yellow Ribbon Singapore (YRSG) have continued to enhance their efforts in these areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: First, more inmates will benefit from Workplace Literacy and Numeracy (WPLN) certification, which is a recognised qualification for employment and upskilling opportunities in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Third, Career Resource Centres have been set up in prisons to allow pre-release inmates to access career-related materials, prepare their resume, submit job applications and attend career talks, empowering inmates to take ownership of their employment journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This expands on the present framework of career retention support provided by YRSG.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: By enhancing inmates' readiness for employment, we encourage a personal commitment to positive change, leading to sustained reintegration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Successful reintegration also depends on employers' preparedness to hire ex-offenders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: YRSG conducts structured onboarding sessions with new employers and monitors the effectiveness of our partnership with employers through regular engagement sessions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, Project Beyond Hiring trains and equips workplace supervisors with the skills needed to manage ex-offenders effectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This complements YRSG's career retention support and better prepares employers to integrate ex-offenders into their workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Patrick Tay asked if the spent regime for criminal records could be reviewed to support ex-offenders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our current assessment is that the regime remains appropriate and fair in striking a balance between rehabilitation and reintegration of ex-offenders, and the interest of potential employers and society at large.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Beyond enhancing inmates' economic capital, it is important to build their social capital, through strengthening ties with the family, and developing pro-social networks in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The FAMily Engagement model (FAME) was launched to strengthen inmates' relationship with the family, to support longer term desistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As part of FAME, SPS developed the "Together in Every Step" – it is a programme where every inmate will attend upon admission to identify their family needs and be matched with relevant programmes and services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: SPS will implement the Peer Engagement and Empowered Rehabilitation Support Framework to strengthen the existing community of prosocial inmates and desistors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Suitable inmates have been trained as peer supporters and will further develop their skills by co-facilitating motivational and psychological correctional programmes with SPS staff.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Upon release, these peer supporters can join the Desistor Network community to further develop their skills in this area through participation in desistor support groups and continuous learning.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Initiatives under the Yellow Ribbon Project (YRP) will be enhanced in 2026 to continue advancing community partnerships and inspire community support for ex-offenders' rehabilitation and reintegration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: YRP will revitalise its flagship events to attract new audiences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, the Yellow Ribbon Prison Run will hold its inaugural city run in 2026.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Participants will experience a scenic route around the National Stadium, culminating in a vibrant end-point carnival that brings communities together to celebrate second chances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The YRP message will be amplified through strategic partnerships with well-established brands and organisations that share our vision for an inclusive society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our community partners are key in inmates' rehabilitation and reintegration journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: SPS continues to increase its engagement with community partners to equip them to better support inmates after their release through structured and tiered training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I will now speak in Malay on the role of Malay/Muslim Organisations (MMOs) in our rehabilitation efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In Mandarin):   MHA collaborates closely with various Malay/Muslim and Indian/Muslim organisations (MMOs) for the rehabilitation and reintegration of inmates and ex-offenders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This is because the MMOs are more attuned to the community’s cultural nuances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In 2024, “Next Lap” project groups were formed under the MMO Rehabilitation Network (MMORN) to better understand the needs of families, inmates and youths-at-risk.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This project group brings together MHA and MMOs to identify gaps and propose ground-up recommendations to enhance assistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The work of the project groups is still in progress, and we expect to announce the full set of recommendations at the MMORN Forum to be held later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Some of their preliminary recommendations include a hotline dedicated to support families of inmates and ex-offenders, as well as a one-stop rehabilitation hub to consolidate the MMO programmes and initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In English): Sir, MHA has enhanced the culture-responsive rehabilitation for the Indian offender population.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: SPS collaborates with SINDA to provide assistance to Indian inmates and their families.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: SPS has also collaborated with FITRAH and Abdul Gafoor Mosque to provide faith-based mentorship for Indian/Muslim inmates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: SPS' efforts to engage and build more partnership with Indian organisations is guided by Senior Minister of State Murali Pillai.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This will help to enhance the rehabilitation and reintegration of Indian offenders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue to achieve even better rehabilitation and reintegration outcomes and reduce re-offending.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: But to succeed, we need everyone's support across society to give second chances to our ex-offenders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Chairman, over the years, the Home Team has initiated many transformation efforts, so that even with manpower constraints and constantly evolving security challenges, we can keep Singapore and Singaporeans safe.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Today, I will speak on how the Home Team plans to continue transforming.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will press on with leveraging smart and autonomous technologies across Home Team departments in 2026.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: PROTECT is able to patrol autonomously and can be remotely operated to mitigate potential hazards during incident response.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mobile users will not have to download any apps to receive SG Alert notifications.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We believe this capability will significantly enhance Singaporeans' preparedness for serious emergencies, such as major fire, chemical or terror incidents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: At selected self-help kiosks, the SPF has started using the Report Lodging Co-Pilot (R-COP), an AI-enabled chatbot which prompts members of the public for relevant information when making Police reports.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This makes the reports clearer and more complete, reducing the need for follow-up calls from the Investigating Officer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Since its roll-out at seven Police divisional headquarters from October 2025, over 90% of users gave positive feedback.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Many found the chatbot easy to use and agreed that it helped to make reports more accurate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Police will roll out R-COP to more self-help kiosks by the middle of the year and continue to improve user experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: R-COP, alongside SPF's other investments in technology, has also helped the SPF to be more efficient in deploying limited Police resources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, through the unmanning of some service counters and the merging of selected NPCs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The merging of NPCs aims to optimise limited Police resources by combining smaller NPCs serving contiguous areas into a larger operational base.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Doing so enhances deployment flexibility and supports response to more complex incidents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There will be no change in Police presence and response time to incidents in estates served by merged NPCs, including responsiveness to 999 calls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Since 2022, SPF has smoothly carried out three mergers at NPCs in Bedok, Yishun and Bukit Batok.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will continue to work closely with community partners, residents and other stakeholders to ensure seamless transition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong spoke about the importance of AI in his Budget speech.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have been prioritising AI as an enabler for developing Home Team capabilities and launched the Home Team AI Movement two years ago.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari asked for an update on our AI efforts and how we are safeguarding the use of AI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HTX has also developed an AI training roadmap and launched upskilling programmes to nurture AI interest and develop AI skills in all Home Team officers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is a data-secure and self-contained model developed by HTX, which is trained on Singapore and Home Team data and does not require Internet connectivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Phoenix paves the way for us to develop AI solutions tailored to the Home Team's operational needs and for purposes which are security-classified.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Significant computing power is required to develop AI applications and train models.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To address this, HTX has built the Next Generation Infrastructure (NGINE), MHA's first enterprise-grade AI infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: NGINE hosts the Home Team's AI applications and provides an important boost in scaling AI deployment for the Home Team.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The first phase was launched in 2025, and the infrastructure will be scaled up progressively as the Home Team expands AI capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Building an AI-ready workforce and NGINE will enable HTX to accelerate AI deployment across the Home Team.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: One example is R-COP, which I had mentioned earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Another example is the Central Narcotics Bureau's NarcoNet.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is a multimodal AI platform to accelerate investigative processes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There is also the Immigration and Checkpoint Authority's MATRIX, which leverages vision language AI models for greater accuracy in document classification and data extraction from documents submitted by applicants for immigration facilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Sanjeev asked about the integration of AI-enabled and humanoid robots into frontline operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Such robots can reduce Home Team officers' exposure to higher-risk environments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are working on this and aim to share our plans in the coming months.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: While we press ahead with AI, we are mindful that AI solutions must be trustworthy and delivered responsibly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As with other technologies, AI comes with risks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So, in 2025, we refreshed our AI Governance Framework and established a playbook alongside it to guide the responsible development, deployment and use of AI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HTX will also deploy AI guardrails-as-a-service to protect our AI solutions from attacks and ensure that output is safe and reliable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Another area in which we are investing heavily in technology is road safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These cameras will strengthen our traffic policing capabilities once fully operationalised in the first quarter of this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We need a stronger enforcement posture because our roads are becoming less safe.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Traffic violations have also been on an upward trend, increasing by about 38% from 2021 to 2025.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This unwelcome trend has occurred despite constant efforts to improve road safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MHA has been working closely with MOT and the Land Transport Authority to design our road infrastructure in a manner that promotes and demands safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Traffic Police has been stepping up presence, enforcement and public engagement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have rolled out more cameras to detect violations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Beyond enforcement by the Traffic Police, Ground Response Force officers who come across traffic violations will also take enforcement action, supplemented by technology, such as their in-vehicle video recording system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will continue enforcement, but we also need to look beyond enforcement to reverse these trends decisively because accidents, injuries and fatalities can all be prevented.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is possible to achieve zero road fatalities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: From early July 2024 to early July 2025, Helsinki recorded zero road traffic fatalities for an entire year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They have been a strong proponent of Vision Zero, an approach that aims to eliminate all traffic deaths and serious injuries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There is no reason why we cannot aspire to zero road fatalities here in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But it requires collective recognition that our road culture needs to change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Now, it is true that life moves at a fast pace in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It can be all too easy to disregard traffic rules or the needs of other road users, especially when we are rushing for time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Giving way does not seem to come as naturally to us as making sure that we do not concede any advantage to other road users.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ask any group of road users and we are likely to be told that the problem lies with other groups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: When we talk to drivers, they will point out that motorcyclists, cyclists or pedestrians are at fault.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If we talk to motorcyclists, we are likely to be told that it is the drivers who are the problem, and so on and so forth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But it may well be that everyone is right, and that all of us – drivers, riders and pedestrians – all have to commit to making changes in our habits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Otherwise, our road safety situation is not going to improve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ms Cassandra Lee asked about how we can keep our families safe on the roads by strengthening road safety awareness and rules.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In the coming months, MHA and the Traffic Police will work with partners on a new and sustained public engagement campaign on road safety, addressing all categories of road users.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We hope to have the support of Members of this House.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: At the same time, we will make further changes to our enforcement posture, starting with drink-driving.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They put themselves and others at great risk.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There have been many horrific accidents caused by drunk drivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our drink driving limit today is 35 micrograms of alcohol per 100 millilitres of breath.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This brings us in line with other jurisdictions in Asia, such as Taiwan, Japan and South Korea.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The message is simple: if you drink, do not drive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Legislative amendments will be made later this year to effect the changes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I agree with her that the penalties should be higher in cases where a driver puts another person in danger on purpose, as in Jarrett Tee's case.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will study this with a view towards introducing a new offence to tackle such behaviour, with a higher maximum penalty than the existing offence of dangerous driving causing death.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Chairman, everyone must play our part to keep our roads safe.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This may include reducing the number of demerit points that can be accumulated before a driver is suspended and also increasing the suspension periods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But it may be necessary, in order to arrest the deteriorating situation, increase deterrence and keep dangerous motorists off the roads.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We know that time is needed for attitudes and behaviours to change, which is why we will engage stakeholders and members of the public to co-create solutions on what more can be done to improve our traffic safety situation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will also give due consideration to the perspectives of vocational drivers, having consulted the transport-related unions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Another group that we are concerned with is foreign-registered vehicles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Whether they are on our roads for economic reasons or for leisure, they have a significant collective presence, so there is also a need to strengthen deterrence and enforcement against violations by foreign-registered vehicles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are working on several measures and will announce the details when ready.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Chairman, please let me conclude this segment of my speech in Mandarin.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Chairman, our roads have become increasingly unsafe.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Despite our continued introduction of stricter regulatory measures, traffic fatalities and traffic violation cases continue to rise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Besides continuing to strengthen enforcement, we must also go beyond enforcement and decisively reverse this trend, because traffic accidents and the casualties can all be prevented.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Singapore's pace of life is fast, and most road users are in a hurry and are easily distracted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In such circumstances, people easily ignore traffic rules or overlook the safety of other road users.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Road users comprise different groups, including motorists, motorcyclists, cyclists, pedestrians and others.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We often hear individual groups complaining that the other groups of road users do not follow traffic rules.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In fact, regardless of what mode of transport is being used, every road user must adjust their habits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Otherwise, road safety will be difficult to improve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our main consideration is to reduce dangerous driving and curb the deteriorating road safety situation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will also give due consideration to the perspectives of vocational drivers, having consulted the transport-related unions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, the Home Team increasingly has to do more with less.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: That is why we must fully exploit the opportunities today's technology affords us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Doing so allows us to maintain high levels of effectiveness, to continue to keep Singapore safe and secure.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: According to the Global Anti-Scam Alliance, scammers globally stole over $1.26 trillion in 2025.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: In Singapore, we have been striking back at scammers, and the scams situation in Singapore improved last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: And together with its partners, the SPF helped victims avert at least another $339 million in potential losses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Anyone can fall prey, the young, old, from all walks of life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked about law enforcement's response to scam victims who may suffer psychological distress.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: To support them, the Police may refer them to the Victim Care Cadre Programme where Victim Care Officers, or VCOs, provide psychological first aid and crisis intervention.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: The VCOs may also refer the victims to community and professional resources for longer-term psychological and financial support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Members will know that while the Victim Care Cadre Programme is available for all victims, it would generally require consent for their participation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Last year, more than 150 victims had taken up the programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Even for cases where the VCOs are not activated, the Police will provide information on the community support options and the steps that victims could take if they fall prey to scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim also asked about the guidelines on updating victims on the status of investigations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Victims will receive an acknowledgement letter or email within seven days after the report is lodged.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: As every case is unique and the time to investigate each case defers, the Police will then update the victims when there are significant developments to the case.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: As Mr Vikram Nair mentioned, the highly sophisticated use of AI and social engineering by scammers is of concern.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: For example, the Police have seen scammers impersonating high-ranking executives and Government officials using deepfakes in live video calls and instructing the victims to transfer funds under the pretext of business payments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Despite the overall decrease in scam cases and losses last year, more Singaporeans fell prey to Government officials Impersonation Scams (GOIS).

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: It is among the top five most reported scam types in 2025.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: MHA has taken upstream steps to curb GOIS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Since September 2025, we issued four Online Criminal Harms Act (OCHA) Implementation Directives to Meta, Apple and Google.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: The Implementation Directives issued to Meta in September 2025 and January 2026 required Meta to implement measures to remove scam advertisements, accounts, profiles and pages that impersonate Singapore Government office holders and persons assessed by the SPF to be at high risk of being impersonated.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: For Apple and Google, the Implementation Directives were issued to them in November 2025 to require them to put in place measures to prevent spoofing of Government agencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Meta has put in place measures required in the Implementation Directive issued in September 2025.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: The SPF is assessing the platforms' compliance with the Implementation Directives issued in November 2025 and January 2026.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: This year, we will require online platforms to put in place more anti-scam measures, as Dr Wan Rizal asked about.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Similar to Apple and Google, we will soon require WhatsApp to implement measures against the spoofing of "gov.sg" and Singapore Government agencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We will also help Singaporeans identify legitimate calls from Government agencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: The SPF is working with Open Government Product and the Infocomm Media Development Authority to introduce a single, easily recognisable prefixed number which all SPF officers will use to call members of the public.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Going forward, if you receive an unknown phone call and the caller claims to be a SPF officer, it is likely a scam.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: My colleague from MDDI, Minister of State Jasmin Lau, will share more details about this measure and its implementation across Government agencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Ms Kuah Boon Theng, Mr Alex Yeo, Ms Cassandra Lee and Mr Vikram Nair spoke about legislative levers to allow the Government to take more decisive action against perpetrators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Members will be aware that many scammers are based overseas and have exploited local mules to perpetrate their crimes in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: This is why we have introduced several new offences to punish mules.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: In 2025, we operationalised the offences criminalising the misuse of SIM cards.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Since then, the SPF has charged 79 offenders under the new offences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We also introduced caning to punish scammers and mules.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: This is necessary given the harms they cause to victims and for strong deterrence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: But those who are deceived into being scam mules will not be penalised with caning.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: MHA will work with the interagency Sentencing Advisory Panel to introduce sentencing guidelines for the misuse of SIM cards.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: These sentencing guidelines will provide a framework on the factors to be considered in sentencing, to ensure that the sentences meted out for egregious cases are sufficiently deterrent.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked about the Government’s assessment of the efficacy of OCHA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: OCHA enables the Police to direct online service providers to disable access to online criminal content like scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Online service providers have acted on all directions, generally within 24 hours.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: OCHA also allows the Government to direct online platforms to implement measures that we believe are necessary to prevent scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We could not do this prior to OCHA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: In essence, OCHA strengthens the Government's ability to tackle online criminal content and has contributed to the improved scam situation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Notwithstanding, scammers continue to approach victims predominantly through online platforms, like Facebook and Carousell.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Accounts on these online platforms are often obtained through fraudulent means.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: For example, people relinquishing their Singpass-verified Carousell accounts to scammers to make a quick buck.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: MHA will adopt a multipronged approach to tackle this.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: First, as Dr Wan Rizal mentioned, we will work with online platforms to strengthen anti-scam measures.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: They include enhancing existing OCHA Codes of Practice to require stricter user verification and to impose a response time for platforms to act on user reports on scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Second, MHA is exploring new legislation to enable the Police to enforce against mules who obtain or supply online accounts to facilitate scams and other crimes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Collaboration with our industry partners is a key part of the Government's strategy to fight scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: The improvement in the scam situation in Singapore would not have been possible without our industry partners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: The co-location of representatives from seven major banks at the Anti-Scam Centre has allowed the SPF to stop scam transactions more effectively.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Dr Wan Rizal asked about the Government's plans to work even more closely with the private sector while Ms Kuah Boon Theng asked about systemic changes to provide more tools to combat scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Mr Vikram Nair spoke about harnessing technology to improve our response to scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: One feedback that our partners have raised is that they lack the information to detect and disrupt scam-related activities upstream, before the transactions take place and the monies are lost.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: To overcome this challenge, MHA has started sharing more data with our partners and we have seen the benefits.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: For example, in October 2025, Carousell identified more than 250 scam accounts from SPF's sharing of suspicious mobile numbers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: To fully reap the benefit of such data sharing, HTX and the SPF are developing a platform known as the National Scams List.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: That will facilitate the automatic real-time exchange of information between the Government and our partners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: This will provide our partners with additional information on known scam enablers, such as bank accounts, phone lines, online accounts as well as the identity of culprits behind these scam enablers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: With this information, the banks can proactively uncover and suspend more potential scam enablers even before they are used for scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: The banks can then share information on these enablers with the Police, who can in turn investigate further and identify even more scam enablers, thereby enhancing the overall effectiveness of our anti-scam efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We will be introducing legislation later this year to enable and safeguard these data sharing arrangements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked about the state of collaboration with our international and regional partners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Mr Alex Yeo asked if there are any plans to expand FRONTIER+.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: They are the result of years of intelligence sharing through international platforms like FRONTIER+, which has expanded from an alliance of anti-scams units in six jurisdictions in 2024 to now covering 13 jurisdictions across four continents, with countries like Canada, Australia and South Africa joining us in the past year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Specific to ASEAN, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brunei are part of the network.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: The setup of FRONTIER+, mooted by the SPF, has also expedited fund tracing and recovery transnationally.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Leveraging this platform, two iterations of Operation FRONTIER+ were carried out in 2025, resulting in approximately $28.2 million seized from over 36,000 frozen bank accounts in seven jurisdictions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Countries increasingly realise that they must cooperate if they want to deal with scams more decisively in their own jurisdiction.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: The Government will leverage this momentum to actively seek out collaboration opportunities, including encouraging more countries to join FRONTIER+.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Closer to home, we are also stepping up collaboration within the region.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: As the ASEAN Lead Shepherd for Cybercrime, Singapore has worked with fellow members states to develop the Cybercrime Roadmap since 2022.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Arising from the roadmap, at the ASEAN Ministerial Meeting on Transnational Crime in September 2025, Singapore tabled an ASEAN Declaration on Cybercrime and Online Scams to deepen law enforcement coordination to tackle cybercrimes and online scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Mr Vikram Nair and Ms Cassandra Lee spoke about the need to strengthen public education and foster greater personal responsibility and digital vigilance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: A vigilant and well-informed public is truly our most important and final line of defence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We have seen encouraging signs that the public has been adopting the Add, Check, Tell (ACT) mindset.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Through the application, the public can report scam-related phone numbers, SMSes and emails, so we can take action and warn others about them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: In other words, by using the application, you not only protect yourself from scams, you also prevent a fellow Singaporean from being the next victim.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: The public can also call and check with the 24/7 ScamShield Helpline at 1799 when they are unsure if something is a scam.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Today, the helpline receives about 500 calls daily and around 85% are made to check on a potential scam.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to conclude my speech with some comments in Mandarin.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: (In Mandarin):   The scam situation in 2025 has improved compared to 2024.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Among these, impersonation of Government official cases has increased and the average loss per case exceeds $72,000, which is of particular concern to us.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: The victims of such scam cases are mostly seniors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: So, I hope to remind the seniors to be especially vigilant.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: If in doubt, please call the ScamShield hotline 1799 to verify.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: The Government is determined to work with Singaporeans to combat scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: In 2026, we will address the issue at source by working with industry partners to introduce anti-scam measures, such as implementing stricter user identity verification and preventing criminals from impersonating Government officials.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We will strengthen investigation and strengthen enforcement efforts through cooperation with international partners, leveraging technology to identify and combat scam activities at their roots.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We will also strengthen legislation, including authorising the Police to take action against money mules who abuse online accounts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Here, I would like to appeal to Singaporeans to download ScamShield and do their part in the fight against scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: ScamShield's functions include setting up features on your mobile phone to block scam calls and filter scam text messages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: After verification by the authorities, these numbers will be added to the blocked list to prevent more people from becoming victims.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: You can protect you and your loved ones from scam harm.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: Scams are very difficult to eradicate because they prey on human emotions and our lifestyles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: But we must also make it very difficult for the perpetrator to get their way.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: The Government has for several years now built defences across the lifecycle of a scam.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: From upstream prevention to more efficient and coordinated enforcement and asset recovery.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: From tougher laws and penalties against the bad actors to extensive education to inform and inoculate the public.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
text: We remain committed to this mission to better protect Singaporeans against scams.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I understand that more scams are now being committed through cryptocurrencies because of the tighter framework we have around bank accounts.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Is the Government concerned about scams perpetuated through cryptocurrencies?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Are they implementing any measures to deal with this new type of scam?

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: In recent years, the Government has observed scammers pivoting to cryptocurrency as a new money-laundering conduit.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Scammers exploit the speed and ease of crypto transactions to frustrate the Police's asset recovery efforts.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: They also make use of the anonymity features of certain crypto transactions to hide their trails.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: This shift in modus operandi is evident from the SPF's annual statistics on scams, which was released recently.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: As the Member mentioned, scammers do make use of the public's relative unfamiliarity – given that crypto is still fairly new, relatively speaking – to induce victims to make fiat transfers to crypto accounts.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: One case that I know about involved a 75-year-old man who fell victim to an investment scam after seeing a deepfake video of a Singapore Minister, one of our Ministers, endorsing a crypto scheme.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: He was added to a WhatsApp group and was convinced by group discussions and the fake video to invest over $4,000 from his Central Provident Funds.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has been working with regulated digital payment token service providers to strengthen their anti-scam controls.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Measures include stepping up fraud surveillance to detect mule accounts and introducing friction and anti-scam warnings to safeguard crypto account holders.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: On MHA's end, the SPF has also built up its cryptocurrency competencies.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: A crypto tracing team was established in the Anti-Scam Command since March last year.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: The team has since followed up on over 1,800 cases involving the dissipation of cryptocurrencies associated with scams.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Leveraging on advanced blockchain analytics and a network of industry partners, the team successfully recovered cryptocurrencies valued at approximately $22.8 million.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: But as I mentioned earlier, a vigilant public is still the most important line of defence.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: I urge all members of the public to think twice.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: When an unknown third party asks you to send money, especially via crypto for investment opportunities, always check the claim and ask ourselves, is this legitimate?

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Should I call 1799 to check if this is a scam?

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: The old maxim remains true, including in crypto: "if it sounds too good to be true, it probably is".

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But we do have measures, which we have put in place, including assisting with the elderly and the mobility impaired.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: First of all, we have a building design that is in coherence with the Fire Code.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In this Fire Code, each unit is designed to be a compartment in itself.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That helps to retard the spread of fire.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In addition, the common corridors have natural ventilation – that is the design intent – provided, of course, the common corridors are free from clutter.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That is something that I think we all can help to see to.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Second, beyond high-rise buildings complying with the Fire Code, there are also what we call "super high-rise buildings" and these are 40 storeys and above.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For that, additional measures, such as having wet rising mains and having at least two fire lifts.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: All of this helps SCDF in their firefighting measures, rescue measures and these facilities are maintained by the Town Council or the Management Corporation Strata Title (MCST) where appropriate.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: If you put this together, then the evacuation protocols by SCDF can be better carried out.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In the SCDF protocols, SCDF prioritises the evacuation of the occupants on the floor affected by the fire and the two floors above.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The usual instruction is for residents in the unaffected floors to remain in their units and SCDF will assess on the ground whether evacuation is necessary.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For those who require special assistance and those who cannot or are unable to evacuate themselves independently, they should stay in their own unit or in a room that is furthest away from the fire, close the door and as far as possible, inform the authorities of their location and wait for assistance.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So those are the measures both in terms of the design infrastructure as well as the measures that SCDF takes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But ultimately, it is important that we are all prepared as a community.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Having community assistance and support for residents and having the awareness and the wherewithal as well when that happens.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And of course that also includes ensuring that the basic requirements of having a fire blanket or, first, the fire extinguisher present in the homes would be very useful, given that in most of these fire situations, they are caused by unattended fires, cooking fires, cooking on the stove, and these are all pretty commonplace to the extent that for the fires that happen, and a fire blanket in such a situation, or an extinguisher would be very useful as the measure of first resort.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I see a number of hands, I am going to prioritise those who have filed cuts, by the amount of time they have filed.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: On the demand side of drugs, we have seen states that have legalised cannabis.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Thailand, for example, Colorado, for example, and we see a very difficult, an immense difficulty in reversing this.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: We do not wish difficulties on our brother countries, but I think we should learn from this.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: We should learn and emphasise and educate Singaporeans to go easy on recreational drugs, creates a long tail of reversal.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: So could we put the literature out there to say that if you want to go down this route, it is going to be intergenerational harm to reverse it, even if it is reversed.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: That is the demand side of the house.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: On the supply side of the house where drug trafficking is concerned, there have been a number of studies and I would like to ask the Minister whether he would be emphasising the literature where a study was taken out a number of years ago as to whether Singaporeans supported the death penalty for certain offences, including drug trafficking, and there was quite a high degree of support for that.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: There was another separate study which showed that people deliberately trafficked below the capital punishment threshold, which would support the position that our tough drug laws deter.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: So, these should not be wasted opportunities to educate that we have a reasonably comprehensive way of dealing with our zero-drug tolerance attitude and would that go out in the educational realm to Singaporeans?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We not only refer to articles or literature, we also work with our counterparts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Sometimes when we visit them, we also learn from them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We see what is happening around them and we bring some of these learning points back.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, I assure the Member we will do that.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, that is actually from a societal point of view.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But within, especially on the demand side, we have worked, or we are working with desistors who share their experiences with community at large.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Schools, and even parents who are concerned about their children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, we have built an ecosystem whereby we have readily available desistors who avail themselves and are very passionate about reaching out to them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: One is at the national level, but I think equally, I would say, or more important, see how we can navigate this on the ground, where we really, really reach out through the various programme, like Dadah Itu Haram, with the IMC, that we have to prevent youth from taking or using drugs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At the same time, I shared with the Member about the cultural nuancing, Senior Minister of State Murali also going on the ground to reach out to the different communities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, we thank the Member for his strong support, and we hope that he will continue to partner with us and to keep Singapore drug free.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam
text: I have one clarification for Senior Minister of State Faishal.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam
text: Can I ask how is CNB dealing with drugs traded on virtual platforms, like e-commerce marketplaces and encrypted messaging apps?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In fact, we are into this whole system a lot more these days, compared to the time when I first started to join MHA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As I shared in my speech, we take proactive measures to monitor these messaging apps and take actions against those who are really facilitating drug trafficking activities here.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And if you also relate to some of these activities, they originate from overseas, and it is orchestrated by drug syndicates and we spare no effort in taking actions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In fact, we work very closely to share best practices, experiences and intelligence with our counterparts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We work very closely with the Thailand Office of Narcotic Control Board to track down a Singaporean, if you can recollect, Mr Benny Kee Soon Chuan.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: He was involved in a drug trafficking syndicate in Thailand.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The other avenue that come in will be through parcel delivery, Sir.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Parcel delivery, where we also work with ICA and public sector stakeholders, and also major courier companies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: These 166 parcels were suspected to contain drugs or drug-related paraphernalia.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In addition to that, we also enhance the awareness of the legal consequences of drug trafficking or drug abuse, so we continue to do that.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, we take this as something very serious, because we want to protect fellow Singaporeans and to keep Singapore safe and secure.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And there was a question about the death penalty survey.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Yes, this is something that was asked by Christopher de Souza earlier.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is something that we also want to make sure that we get support from Singaporeans, and I must tell you that, because I work actively on the ground, I must say the large majority of Singaporeans continue to want us to have a very strong stance against drugs, and also want us to make sure that we keep themselves, their families safe, and one of the things that they support is the death penalty.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: There is not just a drugs problem, but actually there is also a scam angle to his question.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: I have personally received quite a few messages on platforms, such as Telegram, for example.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: The key thing here is, for many of these victims, because of the nature of the transaction, will also not report this to the authorities.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: So, I would just like to use this opportunity to also highlight to members of the public, especially our youths out there, not to believe such messages when they do receive it.

speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee
text: She mentioned that MHA will be revising the threshold to 15 micrograms of alcohol per 100 millilitres of breath.

speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee
text: I am wondering how MHA arrived at that revised threshold and how MHA intends to enforce this.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We also reviewed scientific studies and limits set by other countries and jurisdictions.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I have a clarification for the Senior Minister of State Sim Ann when she spoke about MHA having to do more with less and having to make transformations to leverage on technology.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, I would like to ask her whether the Ministry also agrees that it is very important that any transformation bears in mind that policing, for example, the services should remain truly accessible to all segments of society.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: To that end, any reorganisation should also take into consideration whether areas have a high concentration of elderly and how much more difficult it would be for them, under the transformation to get to the nearest manned counter, for instance.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We agree with Ms Sylvia Lim that we have to be very sensitive to the varied needs of our population.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: At the end of the day, we have to be very mindful of the need to look after all of Singapore, while at the same time, dealing with manpower constraints.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We will be deploying technology sensitively and always with a view of improving or maintaining safety and security outcomes.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: And this is also the reason why we stay in close touch with the public, so that they are able to also, give us feedback and that we can also adjust our deployment accordingly.

speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam
text: My question pertains to Yellow Ribbon itself, in terms of employment.

speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam
text: We know that the employment ecosystem is very important and in certain sectors actually, each offender before they are released into the system, they undergo interview process and they actually have multiple job offers.

speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam
text: So, I just wanted to know how often is the review of this job review ecosystem and whether it looks at the number of employers.

speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam
text: It is not so important to have that many number of employers, but more important to actually have the ecosystem of care where the case manager, the employer and everyone is included in the aftercare of the ex-offender.

speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam
text: So, I just wanted to know how often is that review done?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: One thing that I would like to share with the Member is that, we not only look at the numbers of the employers that work with us, we look at the process and the effectiveness of the efforts being undertaken like, for example, you look at the type of industries that we have been exposing our inmates to.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We have included new areas of growth and at the same time the kind of jobs that they do.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Also, there is a diversity of that kind of jobs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In addition to that, we have the career coach who will journey with the ex-inmates to see how we can navigate this process of getting a job and having the job and trying to sustain it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We also train the employers, the staff of the organisation, so that they understand and they know how to handle our friends who really, really wanting to get a job and find meaning in the job.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I must say that I am very happy that I have met quite a number of them who, upon release, they may be working with a company, and some would have progress.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Others found an opportunity within the similar industry to continue to progress to another company.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, it is not only about review, we continuously do a review, but we continuously enhance the ecosystem that we have.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We also better prepare the inmates so that they can have not only more opportunities, but they are able to sustain their job.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: You are right to say that one inmate may receive more than one offers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This is something that we want to continue to provide them with the opportunity and at the same time help them, not only provide that beyond second chances – grow as high as they can.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik
text: I welcome the prison services screening process where mental health history collected upon admission to prison or the Drug Rehabilitation Centre (DRC) is then used to tailor individualised rehabilitation programmes for each inmate.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik
text: And finally, a reply to my earlier Parliamentary Questions, stated that Central Narcotics Bureau (CNB) does not collect mental health data on arrested drug abusers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: With due respect, I think the Member may not truly understand the process of how we are able to find out whether the person has mental health.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, at that stage, because of the investigation process and also putting the person in remand, CNB would not have the chance to know if he or she has a mental health issue.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is only when the person enters remand, the prison, then we will assess.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We assess everyone; as I shared in my answer, physical and mental health.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In fact, we have a strong support system in the prison where we not only look after them, we customise their rehab process.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The curriculum that we do for them is different.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In a sense, we want to care for them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We have the data and at the same time, we also work with the community services or organisation, for example, Minds and also IMH, to see how we can help them upon their release.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, this is something that we are not only familiar, we have been doing this for many years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We understand their needs and we want to continue to take care of them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But I must say it is not easy, but we will do our best.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: This is just picking up on a point to do with scams, but also the international aspect of it.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I think a lot of scams originate from abroad and one of the pieces of feedback we have is quite often MHA recovers sums from scams, but the time it takes to reach the victims is quite long.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: It can be a few years; has to go through a disposal hearing and so on.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: So, is MHA considering having some simplified processes so that amounts recovered from scams can be returned to victims more expeditiously?

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Member for the question.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Indeed, it is MHA and SPF priority to try and return the funds as quickly as possible.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: However, in many of these financial crime cases, including cryptocurrency, including scams, the money trace often is very, very complex.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: So, what the Police needs to do is they will freeze all the assets – the bank accounts, the properties – and for as long as it takes to fully investigate and track where the monies come from, they will have to do so.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Only when they have fully resolved and the frozen assets are no longer required to be frozen, can they then apply to the Court for the property to be returned to the rightful owners.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: The key thing here, as much as we want to simplify the process, it is also difficult, because more often at times, many of the seized proceeds and many of the cases are not just about scams.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: It also involves illegal money laundering, legal money lending.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: And therefore, many of times the assets – be it assets, cash or property – are often commingled and therefore, it is actually very difficult for us to directly apportion this amount was from this case and that was from another case.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: That adds to the complexity of scam cases.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: But I acknowledge indeed that this is something the public is keen and, of course, every single victim, and we have many victims, will be keen to see the process being simplified and shortened, and we will look at what else we can do to make it faster and simpler.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr de Souza, you have your hand up again.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I am going to take you and then Ms Yeo Wan Ling.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: In relation to the study on the drug trafficking and the death penalty.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: In fact, in response to that, I think there is a very good statistic that we should elaborate on in this House and also out there in education that 15 grams of diamorphine feeds 180 drug abuses for one week.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Half of them are married, that is 90 spouses, that is 270 people.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: If each of the married couple have one child, that is another 90.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: That is one HDB block that I am responsible for.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: So, I think we have to be harsh with people who come and seek to do damage to lives over intergenerations and statistics like this are key to pursue our zero tolerance position on drugs.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: And I would like to know whether the Minister agrees with the use of statistics in such a forceful way to make an objective and evidentially based position.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We certainly agree with you that we can use more statistics on this.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We have done so and with your suggestion we should do more, and we will do so.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We also recognise that it is an issue that requires a lot of discussion, a lot of justification and winning the hearts and minds of the people.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, it is a journey that we want every Singaporean to be part of the journey and some may not even understand the real consequences, like what you shared earlier.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If you look at it and if the person is your child or your loved ones, you will have a different perspective about this.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, I am very happy to see Members here supporting our effort.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We need fellow Singaporean to support and we need the global community to be on board this journey as well, because then we can save the global community from the scourge of drugs.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: I have a clarification for Senior Minister of State Sim Ann.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Vikram Nair, do you wish to withdraw your amendment.

text: Chairman, I would like to thank Minister Edwin Tong, Senior Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim, Senior Minister of State Sim Ann and Minister of State Goh Pei Ming for sharing with us the Ministry's work.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: And, of course, a big thank you to all the staff at the Ministry, the uniformed personnel.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Of course, in support of the Budget, I will be withdrawing my cut.
